messages.subject: error with facet wrap and stat_bin2d
parts:
I am having some trouble facet wrapping. The dataset is:

> summary(dbhht)
float0 string2 float1
Min. : 1.00 rw :899 Min. : 0.00
1st Qu.:12.00 df :158 1st Qu.: 61.00
Median :20.00 ss :116 Median : 90.00
Mean :20.85 ra : 97 Mean : 87.08
3rd Qu.:28.00 gf : 29 3rd Qu.:113.00
Max. :84.00 wh : 27 Max. :236.55
(Other): 59

i'm able to produce the plot id like for all the data using the
following:

> d <- ggplot(dbhht, aes_string(x='float1', y='float0', group='string2'))
> d + stat_bin2d() + geom_bin2d()

however when I attempt to facet the data using 'string2' in this way
it results in an error:
> d + stat_bin2d() + geom_bin2d() + facet_wrap(~ 'string2')
Error in dim(out) <- c(1, nrow(.$facet_levels)) :
dims [product 1] do not match the length of object [0]

Any guidance would be gratefully accepted.

Peter

messages.author: 065110cca96a6373
messages.subject: Re: error with facet wrap and stat_bin2d
parts:
Hi Peter,

The issue has to do with strings (I provide an example at the end).
The typical way to create your base in ggplot is with aes(), but there
is also the aes_string() function which can handle strings, so you do
not see any issue there. However, aes_string() is just a special
parser to deal with text, so when you pass 'string2' to facet_wrap(),
in essence it cannot find the object. There is an error when trying
to assign dimensions, because the "object" (i.e., string2) is empty.
Unquoting it will fix the problem. I would also generally recommend
using aes() in ggplot(), but you may have a good reason for using
aes_string(), which is fine. You will still need to unquote string2
in your call to facet_wrap(). If you need to pass it as text somehow,
I think you will need to create your own intermediate parser that
converts your text to a formula and then passes that formula to
facet_wrap().

Cheers,

Josh

#### Example data ####
## side note, using dput() on your data is a nice way
## to provide it via email that is easy for both parties to use
set.seed(810)
dat <- data.frame(float0 = abs(rnorm(150, 20, sd = 12)),
float1 = abs(rnorm(150, 90, 35)),
string2 = LETTERS[sample(1:7, 150, TRUE)])
summary(dat) # I tried to make it close to your summary


#### Plots ####
d <- ggplot(dat, aes(x = float1, y = float0, group = string2))
d + stat_bin2d() + geom_bin2d() # works
## Facetted without quotes works
d + stat_bin2d() + geom_bin2d() + facet_wrap(~ string2)

## just to show you can use it with aes_string()
d2 <- ggplot(dat, aes_string(x = 'float1', y = 'float0', group = 'string2'))
d2 + stat_bin2d() + geom_bin2d() + facet_wrap(~ string2)

Im using python (with PyR2) to produce these plots and it seems that
aes_string() is the only possibility as python thinks that the unquoted
string vector names are undefined variables (this could probably be
worked around with more code but aes_string makes it easier).

Thanks again for your thorough response, it makes working with a great
piece of free software even better knowing that there are people out
there willing to answer questions.

Peter

messages.author: 065110cca96a6373
messages.subject: Re: error with facet wrap and stat_bin2d
parts:
Hmm, well here is *a* way to pass a string to facet_wrap(). I have
never used python or PyR2 personally, so I don't know if this will
work in that context (using the same data as before):

d2 <- ggplot(dat, aes_string(x = 'float1', y = 'float0', group = 'string2'))
d2 + stat_bin2d() + geom_bin2d() +

facet_wrap(substitute(~x, list(x=as.name("string2"))))

As you can see, string2 is quoted, but now that is wrapped up in a
list whose value is substituted for x, so that what is finally passed
to facet_wrap() is ~string2.

HTH,

Josh

P.S. You are quite welcome; it is my pleasure to answer questions when I can.

> On Sun, Nov 21, 2010 at 11:53 PM, Joshua Wiley <jwiley...@gmail.com> wrote:
>> Hmm, well here is *a* way to pass a string to facet_wrap().  I have
>> never used python or PyR2 personally, so I don't know if this will
>> work in that context (using the same data as before):
>>
>> d2 <- ggplot(dat, aes_string(x = 'float1', y = 'float0', group = 'string2'))
>> d2 + stat_bin2d() + geom_bin2d() +
>>  facet_wrap(substitute(~x, list(x=as.name("string2"))))
>>
>> As you can see, string2 is quoted, but now that is wrapped up in a
>> list whose value is substituted for x, so that what is finally passed
>> to facet_wrap() is ~string2.

>> Josh

>>> One small follow up on this issue...
>>>
>>> Im using python (with PyR2) to produce these plots and it seems that
>>> aes_string() is the only possibility as python thinks that  the unquoted
>>> string vector names are undefined variables (this could probably be worked
>>> around with more code but aes_string makes it easier).
>>>
>>> Thanks again for your thorough response, it makes working with a great piece
>>> of free software even better knowing that there are people out there willing
>>> to answer questions.

>>> On 11/21/2010 08:44 AM, Joshua Wiley wrote:
>>>>
>>>> Hi Peter,
>>>>
>>>> The issue has to do with strings (I provide an example at the end).
>>>> The typical way to create your base in ggplot is with aes(), but there
>>>> is also the aes_string() function which can handle strings, so you do
>>>> not see any issue there.  However, aes_string() is just a special
>>>> parser to deal with text, so when you pass 'string2' to facet_wrap(),
>>>> in essence it cannot find the object.  There is an error when trying
>>>> to assign dimensions, because the "object" (i.e., string2) is empty.
>>>> Unquoting it will fix the problem.  I would also generally recommend
>>>> using aes() in ggplot(), but you may have a good reason for using
>>>> aes_string(), which is fine.  You will still need to unquote string2
>>>> in your call to facet_wrap().  If you need to pass it as text somehow,
>>>> I think you will need to create your own intermediate parser that
>>>> converts your text to a formula and then passes that formula to
>>>> facet_wrap().
>>>>
>>>> Cheers,
>>>>
>>>> Josh
>>>>
>>>> #### Example data ####
>>>> ## side note, using dput() on your data is a nice way
>>>> ## to provide it via email that is easy for both parties to use
>>>> set.seed(810)
>>>> dat<- data.frame(float0 = abs(rnorm(150, 20, sd = 12)),
>>>>                   float1 = abs(rnorm(150, 90, 35)),
>>>>                   string2 = LETTERS[sample(1:7, 150, TRUE)])
>>>> summary(dat) # I tried to make it close to your summary
>>>>
>>>>
>>>> #### Plots ####
>>>> d<- ggplot(dat, aes(x = float1, y = float0, group = string2))
>>>> d + stat_bin2d() + geom_bin2d() # works
>>>> ## Facetted without quotes works
>>>> d + stat_bin2d() + geom_bin2d() + facet_wrap(~ string2)
>>>>
>>>> ## just to show you can use it with aes_string()
>>>> d2<- ggplot(dat, aes_string(x = 'float1', y = 'float0', group =
>>>> 'string2'))
>>>> d2 + stat_bin2d() + geom_bin2d() + facet_wrap(~ string2)
